column3: The Hebrew calls the inheritance His, rather than their inheritance.
The Hebrew uses singular “him” and “his” where BSB uses plural “they,” “their,” and “them.”
The Hebrew says the giver gives to the priest, rather than expressing the giving passively.
The recipient is singular in the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says He chose him and mentions him and his sons at the end; Levi’s name is not repeated here.
The town is called one of your gates; the Hebrew retains the desire of his soul.
The Hebrew calls the other Levites his brothers.
The Hebrew does not explicitly name money or identify the father as singular.
The Hebrew explicitly says not to learn to do these things.
The Hebrew describes making his son and daughter pass through the fire, rather than explicitly using a sacrifice verb.

The Hebrew says He is driving them out, without explicitly repeating the nations.
The Hebrew says to be blameless with the LORD your God.

The Hebrew separately names your midst and your brothers.
The quoted request is in the singular throughout: my God, I hear, I see, and I die.
